title: Virginia Leaps to No. 1 in Top 25 After Dominant Win Over Arkansas – College Basketball Rankings Update
body:
Virginia’s men’s basketball team vaulted into the top‑10 of the Top 25 & 1 poll on Sunday, leaping to No. 9 after a dominant 85‑62 victory over Arkansas. The win, a decisive statement against John Calipari’s Razorbacks, underscored the Cavaliers’ resurgence under veteran head coach Tony Bennett and highlighted the impact of a core group that returned most of its high‑scoring personnel from a 30‑win campaign last season.

The Cavaliers rolled out a balanced attack that saw all five starters in double figures, with senior guard Thijs De Ridder leading the way with 22 points and five assists. De Ridder, who was the nation’s second‑leading scorer in the previous season, continued to demonstrate his elite shooting touch, converting 10 of 13 shots from the field, including four from beyond the arc. Complementing his scoring, junior forward Kyle Gillespie added 16 points and eight rebounds, while sophomore guard Jalen Cox contributed a steady 12 points and a pair of steals that helped stifle Arkansas’ perimeter game.

Virginia’s defensive identity remained the cornerstone of its success. The Cavaliers forced Arkansas into a 34% field‑goal shooting night and limited the Razorbacks to just 12 points in the paint. Bennett’s hallmark “Pack Line” scheme forced the opposition into contested mid‑range attempts, a strategy that paid dividends as Arkansas struggled to find rhythm against the disciplined Virginia defense. The statistical disparity was stark: Virginia out‑rebounded the Razorbacks 44‑29 and forced 18 turnovers, converting 12 of those into fast‑break points.

The win also marked a significant shift in the national perception of Virginia’s program. After a relatively muted start to the season, the Cavaliers have now compiled a 9‑2 record, with their only losses coming at the hands of top‑five opponents. The return of four of the six leading scorers from last year’s 30‑win squad—De Ridder, Gillespie, Cox, and forward Caleb Miller—has restored continuity and experience that were missing early in the campaign. Coach Bennett emphasized that the team’s chemistry and familiarity with the system have accelerated their growth, allowing them to execute both offensively and defensively at a high level.

Analysts note that Virginia’s ascent in the rankings reflects more than a single impressive win. The Cavaliers have demonstrated an ability to dominate both ends of the floor against a variety of opponents, signaling that they could be a serious contender in the upcoming ACC tournament and potentially the NCAA postseason. Their balanced scoring, efficient three‑point shooting (41% as a team this season), and the continued development of role players like sophomore forward Isaiah Miller suggest depth that can weather the inevitable rigors of March.

Looking ahead, Virginia faces a challenging stretch that includes road games against Louisville and a pivotal matchup with conference powerhouse Duke. Success in those contests will be critical to solidifying their top‑10 status and securing a favorable seed for the NCAA tournament. If the Cavaliers can maintain their defensive intensity and keep their scoring options diversified, they are poised to remain a fixture among the nation’s elite teams as the season progresses.
